name: ajv-schema-compilation-provenance
instr:
Ajv compiles a schema into a function, but nothing records how that function was built. Add an opt-in compilation provenance record that compiled products carry and that survives standalone emission.

The `code` option gains a boolean `provenance` member, normalized beside `optimize` and `regExp`. It defaults to disabled, so it reads back as `false` when omitted and when passed `false`. Enabling it must not warn and must not imply `code.source`.

Two types become public and must be nameable from the draft-07, 2019, 2020, and JTD entry modules. `CompilationProvenance` has seven properties: `id`, the resolved base identifier, or the empty string when the schema declares none; `product`, one of the stable tokens `validate`, `parse`, or `serialize`; the booleans `meta` and `async`; `keywords`, deduplicated and sorted lexicographically; `refs`, an ordered edge array; and `options`. `ProvenanceRef` has `ref` as written in the schema, `resolved` against the base identifier in effect, and `kind`, one of `inline`, `call`, `wrapper`, or `root`.

The keyword list names every schema keyword dispatched to a registered rule while building the function, including keywords from subschemas compiled into it. Edges appear one per reference the reference keyword handled, in resolution order, duplicates retained. A kind is `root` when the target is the root schema being compiled, `call` when an already-compiled environment's function is called directly, `wrapper` when the target is still compilin
